glossary._voice: Informal 'je/jij' throughout (Pinterest's Dutch help center uses 'je'; competitors that mix 'u' and 'je' read as machine-translated). Sentence case in titles and meta descriptions (Dutch does not title-case; H1/H2 are uppercased by CSS anyway). Short imperative sentences: 'Plak de link.' 'Tik op Delen.'
glossary._spelling: Proper noun + noun compounds take a hyphen in running text: Pinterest-link, Pinterest-video, Pinterest-video's, Pinterest-bord, GIF-pin, pin.it-link, ZIP-bestand, MP4-video. Keyword-led H1s/titles may keep the space form people type ('Pinterest video downloaden'); Google treats both the same. Plurals of words ending in a vowel take an apostrophe: video's, foto's, GIF's, dia's. Never 'videos'/'fotos'.

formats.locale: nl (Intl: 'nl-NL'; use 'nl-BE' only if a Belgian variant is ever split out)

formats.dates: Long form '14 oktober 2026' (month lowercase). Numeric: NL '14-10-2026', BE '14/10/2026'. Keep ISO 8601 in JSON-LD.

notes.hreflangReasoning: Use 'nl' (language only), not 'nl-NL'. One Dutch version serves both the Netherlands and Flanders: Pinterest's own Dutch UI is a single locale (help.pinterest.com/nl/), the vocabulary in this niche is identical (NL and BE autocomplete matched for 190 of 210 seeds; the 20 differences were ordering or one extra English suggestion), and every Dutch competitor that sets hreflang uses 'nl'. 'nl-NL' alone would tell Google the page targets only the Netherlands. Pair each kept page reciprocally with its English page (hreflang en + nl + x-default=en). Skipped pages must not emit an nl alternate. Set <html lang='nl'>; BaseLayout currently hard-codes lang='en' and emits only en/x-default alternates.
notes.urlScheme: Prefix /nl/ plus a Dutch slug (/nl/pinterest-video-downloaden). The Dutch home is /nl (no trailing slash, matching normalizeCanonical for non-root paths). Competitors keep English slugs (/nl/pinterest-gif-downloader); a Dutch slug matches the query exactly and is a cheap advantage.
notes.marketReality: Dutch speakers search Pinterest downloading in English as much as in Dutch: 'pinterest video downloader', 'pinterest downloader', 'pinterest pin downloader', 'pinterest 4k', 'pinterest mp3' all return English completions under hl=nl. The English pages will keep catching those, so the Dutch pages should own the Dutch verb phrases (downloaden / opslaan) and the 'hoe ...' questions. Expect lower volume per page than English; the bar for quality is low (competitor nl pages are machine-translated, one has Italian leftovers), so well-written native copy is the main edge.
notes.cannibalizationPlan: Tool page /nl/pinterest-video-downloaden owns 'pinterest video downloaden' (+online/gratis/MP4). Guide /nl/hoe-pinterest-video-downloaden owns the 'hoe ...' questions and laptop/pc. Phone guide /nl/pinterest-video-opslaan owns 'opslaan' + galerij/filmrol. Cross-link all three with distinct anchors.
honestyRisks: Do not localize the English 4K page's '4K ultra quality' or 'original uncompressed' claims. PRODUCT.md: no fake 4K.
Do not carry over the SEO generator page's 'increases user clicks by up to 40%' (an unsupported statistic).
Image quality: the pipeline rewrites blocked 'originals' to 1200x (tests/seo-invariants.entry.ts), so Dutch copy says 'grootste openbare versie', not 'originele resolutie'.
Existing nl heroSubtitle in src/lib/i18n.ts promises '1080p HD-kwaliteit' for everything; soften it to 'in de beste beschikbare kwaliteit'.
Copyright FAQs: describe norms (personal use, credit the maker, ask before reposting); do not give legal advice or cite Dutch 'thuiskopie' law.
iOS Dutch share-sheet labels ('Bewaar video', 'Bewaar in Bestanden') and the iOS 'Geanimeerd' album name came from general knowledge, not a fetched source. Check them on a device before publishing.
implementationGotchas: BaseLayout: <html lang='en'> and hreflang en/x-default are hard-coded. Localized pages need a lang prop and a real alternates list.

BaseLayout breadcrumb name = title.split('—')[0]; keep the em dash in Dutch titles (all kept titles except the how-to question title include it; there the full title becomes the breadcrumb, which is acceptable, or pass an explicit breadcrumb name).
DownloaderForm uses t.downloadButton ('Download MP4') for every variant when lang != 'en', so the board and photo pages would show 'Download MP4'. Dutch needs one submit label per variant.

seo_health_check.py checks every dist HTML: one H1, canonical, JSON-LD, title 30–65 (warning outside 40–62), description 110–160 (warning outside 120–158), img alt. Every validated nl title/description is inside the strict 40–62 / 120–158 band.
SITEMAP_ROUTES test only requires English money paths. Add the /nl paths to the sitemap with xhtml:link alternates.
Translated FAQ answers must also be translated in JSON-LD (faqSchema/howToSchema), not left in English.

typography.glyphCoverage: Checked big-shoulders-display-latin-900 with fontTools: ë ï é è ó ö ü á à ê É Ë Ï Ö Ü ’ ‘ “ ” „ – — € · all present. U+0132/0133 (Ĳ ĳ ligature) are missing, which is fine: always type IJ as two letters (the standard practice).
typography.uppercaseIJ: Headlines are uppercased by CSS; with lang='nl', 'ij' uppercases to 'IJ' correctly. Never use text-transform: capitalize on Dutch (it gives 'Ijs' instead of 'IJs').
typography.lengthExpansion: Keyword-led H1s are length-neutral because 'downloaden' replaces 'Downloader' (measured at 46px: −4% to +1% vs English). The guide H1s are shorter than the English ones (−17% and −25%). Body copy runs about 10–20% longer than English, which matters only in fixed-width chips and stamps: 'AFHAALBON · OPENBARE LINK' measures 147px vs 127px at 14px; stamp 'GEDEELTELIJK' is 70px, so prefer 'DEELS'.
typography.longCompounds: Dutch glues nouns together. At the phone H1 size (46px, 328px line), any single word over ~14 uppercase letters overflows: 'PROFIELFOTODOWNLOADER' measures 451px and competitor-style 'PINTEREST-AFBEELDINGSDOWNLOADER' 653px. Keep H1/H2 words short (the validated H1s' longest run is 'DOWNLOADEN' at 237px), and add hyphens:auto with lang='nl' plus overflow-wrap:anywhere as a safety net on display headings.
typography.apostrophes: Plural apostrophes (VIDEO'S, FOTO'S, GIF'S) render in the gothic; use the typographic ’ in display text. Strip apostrophes from slugs (no apostrophes in any chosen slug).

notes.method: Google autocomplete (suggestqueries client=firefox, hl=nl, gl=nl and gl=be, ie/oe=utf-8), 1.1 s between requests, fetched 2026-10-14; raw lists in evidence.autocomplete.raw. Empty lists mean no completion, which suggests low volume but does not prove zero. Competitor pages fetched directly (title/description/H1/H2/H3/hreflang).
